title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model error. A person with legitimate access to a law enforcement tool is accused of querying it for a purpose it was not deployed for, repeatedly and over an extended period. The Flock camera system and the other databases named were built to serve police work, and the alleged failure is that one officer's access was not constrained to that work.

The place in the deployment where this happened is the query layer, the point at which an authorised user turns a system built for one purpose to a private one. Catching it would have required auditing who searched for whom and why, and treating a pattern of searches for one person as a signal rather than as routine traffic. The facts do not establish what logging or review was in place at the Stow department.

The accusation is not a finding. The criminal complaint, the internal affairs outcome, the leave status and the pending Select Board hearing are process, not proof of intent or of guilt, and no court has ruled on the allegation.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of using police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended their abusive relationship about five years ago and changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location through the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 and placed him on paid administrative leave in July. After a four-week internal affairs investigation, he was moved to unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has obtained a restraining order lasting at least a year. The police chief said a Select Board hearing will be held next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
